newsitem.title: Singapore: ASIAN EXOTICS - Offshore demand drives baht higher.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Offshore demand drives baht higher.

text.p: * Thai baht shoots to 13-year high offshore as players scramble to cover short positions established during speculative attack in mid-May. Forwards volatile.
* Malaysian ringgit seen weakening to 2.5200 against dollar on continued poor sentiment after bad trade data.
* Indonesian rupiah, swaps stable amid adequate liquidity.
* Singapore dollar sluggish, gains capped by commercial bank demand around 1.4250/dollar.
The Thai baht shot to a 13-year high in offshore markets on Tuesday as players scrambled to cover short positions established a month ago when the baht came under speculative attack.

The baht was quoted at 23.550/23.650 to the dollar at 0415 GMT after rising to 23.460/24.560 earlier, its highest level since the last baht devaluation in 1984. The baht was traded at 24.250/24.300 late on Monday in the offshore market.
Offshore players, faced with a severe fund shortage due to the Thai central bank's imposition of capital controls in mid-May, sold dollars at a high premium to acquire baht.
"People are still trying to square off the shorts set up during the crisis," a Singapore-based dealer said.
He said the baht was unlikely to strengthen beyond 23.00 to the dollar and looked capped around 23.50 for the day.
The baht/dollar one-month swap premium surged to 160/180 satangs per dollar offshore at 0415 GMT from 100/110 late on Monday.
"The forwards are very firm, especially the short-dates, and that has dragged up the terms as well," the dealer said.
He said offshore parties seemed to be taking advantage of the sharp rise in short-dates to arbitrage against longer tenures.
"That's why you see a swing now. The terms are being taken up whereas the shorter dates are being offered," he said.
"But if they are able to do that, I think a lot of them couldn't be short," he added.
In Malaysia, the ringgit was dented by early dollar demand out of Sydney and then maintained a soft stance due to lingering concerns about poor trade data released last week.
Malaysia announced a trade deficit of 2.1 billion ringgit for April after a 1.75 billion ringgit surplus in March.
A European bank dealer in Kuala lumpur said dollar/ringgit looked set to test a long-standing barrier at 2.5200 and could see a minor break to 2.5220.
Selling of the ringgit/Singapore dollar cross also weighed on the Malaysian unit, dealers said.
The Singapore dollar had a quiet morning, remaining firm below the 1.4300 level to the U.S. dollar due to uncertainty in the baht and weakness in the dollar/majors.
"Dollar/Sing is being capped below the 1.4300 level because of unrest in the regionals. So people are using the Sing as a safe haven to park their funds," a dealer said.
But he said the Sing dollar's gains were being limited by demand for the U.S. unit around 1.4250 and local bank buying around 1.4210/20, believed to be on behalf of the central bank.
"We're now in an effective 1.42-1.43 range," he said.
The Indonesian rupiah continued to trade sluggishly amid adequate liquidity conditions.
Dealers said the dollar looked capped around the 2,430 level amid signs of capital inflows to the Indonesian stock market, where the key index broke the 700 points barrier on Monday.
Spot rupiah was at 2,428.0/29.0 at 0415 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,427.5/28.5.
Dealers said fears of a swap squeeze similar to Thailand's continued to linger in the forward market, prompting foreign parties to maintain long forward positions.
-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221 384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
